stem: Jacques is a chef. He claims that 90% of his customers are satisfied with his cooking. Marie suspects that the true percentage is lower than 90%. She asks a random sample of 15 of Jacques’ customers whether they are satisfied. She then performs a hypothesis test of the null hypothesis $p = 0.9$ against the alternative hypothesis $p < 0.9$, where $p$ is the population proportion of customers who are satisfied. She decides to reject the null hypothesis if fewer than 12 customers are satisfied.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: In the context of the question, explain what is meant by a Type I error.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Find the probability of a Type I error in Marie’s test.
